{{Short description|American chemist}}
'''Bruce H. Lipshutz''' (born 1951) is an American chemist. He is a professor at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chem.ucsb.edu/people/faculty/lipshutz/index.shtml|title=People &#124; Department of Chemistry - UC Santa Barbara|website=www.chem.ucsb.edu}}</ref><!-- Deleted image removed: [[Image:Bhl.jpg|thumb|right|border|Bruce H. Lipshutz]] -->

==Biography==
Lipshutz received his undergraduate degree in chemistry from [[Binghamton University]] in 1973. His graduate work was supervised by [[Harry H. Wasserman]] at [[Yale]].  After a PhD degree in 1977, he spent two years at [[Harvard]] as a post-doctoral researcher in the group of Nobel Laureate [[E. J. Corey]]. Soon after, he accepted a position of Assistant Professor at [[UCSB]] rising to the ranks of Professor in 1987. He has received the [[Alfred P. Sloan Foundation]] Fellowship and the Camille & Henry Dreyfus Teacher-Scholar Award. In 2011 he was awarded Presidential Green Chemistry Award.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.epa.gov/gcc/pubs/pgcc/past.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120803101416/http://www.epa.gov/gcc/pubs/pgcc/past.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 3, 2012|title=Past Award Entries and Recipients &#124; Green Chemistry &#124; US EPA|accessdate=12 August 2023}}</ref>  He is Co-founder of Zymes LLC.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.zymesllc.com/about/management-team/|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080717023707/http://www.zymesllc.com/about/management-team/|url-status=dead|title=Zymes llc|archivedate=July 17, 2008}}</ref>

===Methodologies===
*Higher-order organocuprates (Lipshutz cuprates).<ref>{{Cite journal |doi=10.15227/orgsyn.069.0080  |doi-access=free|title=Mixed higher-order cyanocuprate-induced epoxide openings: 1-benzyloxy-4-penten-2-ol |journal=Organic Syntheses |date=1990 |volume=69 |page=80 }}</ref>

*Catalyst development for ppm Pd-catalyzed C-C couplings in water at ambient<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{cite journal |url=https://pubs.rsc.org/en/Content/ArticleLanding/2018/GC/C8GC01356J|doi=10.1039/C8GC01356J|title=Evan ''Phos'': A ligand for ppm level Pd-catalyzed Suzuki–Miyaura couplings in either organic solvent or water|year=2018|last1=Landstrom|first1=Evan B.|last2=Handa|first2=Sachin|last3=Aue|first3=Donald H.|last4=Gallou|first4=Fabrice|last5=Lipshutz|first5=Bruce H.|journal=Green Chemistry|volume=20|issue=15|pages=3436–3443|url-access=subscription}}</ref>
*Use of nonionic amphiphiles for transition metal-mediated cross coupling in organic synthesis.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/ifb/acta/v41/acta-vol41-2008.html#73/z |title=Merck KGaA |access-date=2019-06-16 |archive-date=2016-11-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161112033834/http://www.sigmaaldrich.com/ifb/acta/v41/acta-vol41-2008.html#73/z |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* Low-cost synthesis of [[Coenzyme Q10]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nsf.gov/od/lpa/news/02/tip021129.htm|title=NSF - OLPA - News Tip: November 29, 2002|website=www.nsf.gov}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |doi = 10.1021/ol051329y|pmid = 16146360|title = An Improved Synthesis of the "Miracle Nutrient" Coenzyme Q10|journal = Organic Letters|volume = 7|issue = 19|pages = 4095–4097|year = 2005|last1 = Lipshutz|first1 = Bruce H.|last2 = Lower|first2 = Asher|last3 = Berl|first3 = Volker|last4 = Schein|first4 = Karin|last5 = Wetterich|first5 = Frank}}</ref>
